title: Police believe 'body' found in suitcase by road was a sex doll

By Isla Evans

Topic:Police

Police at the scene where the suitcase was found at Wolgon Road at Oallen. (ABC News)

Police sources have told the ABC that a "body" found in a suitcase in southern NSW bushland is believed to be a sex doll.

Police initially believed the suitcase, which was found on Sunday afternoon at Oallen, contained the remains of a woman's body.

Police have defended the investigation, saying the correct processes were followed.

Police believe a "body" found in an abandoned suitcase by a dirt road in southern NSW was actually a sex doll.

It was initially feared the abandoned luggage, which was found by members of the public on Sunday afternoon at Oallen, about 60 kilometres south-east of Goulburn, contained a woman's remains.

NSW Police released a statement confirming the remains were not human.

"Following forensic examinations … police confirmed the item located in the bag was a life-like doll, wearing clothing, with hair and a nose piercing," it said.

Commander of the Hume Police District, Superintendent Linda Bradbury, has defended the actions of the officers sent to the scene.

She said there were "no regrets at all" as the correct processes were followed during the investigation.

"The idea is to not disturb crime scenes as much as possible to maintain the integrity of our investigation," Superintendent Bradbury said.

"We've been able to collect the remains, and then take them to investigation at forensics to then determine that they are not human.

"We followed our processes … to a high level and I think it's no regrets all."

Superintendent Linda Bradbury says officers followed police processes. (ABC News: Simon Beardsell)

Police commenced investigations around 1pm on Sunday afternoon, with the remains only confirmed to not be human more than 20 hours later.

Superintendent Bradbury said forensics officers inspected the remains at the scene on Sunday before the suitcase was seized for further examination.

Authorities first established a crime scene on Sunday afternoon after they were called to roadside bushland near Wolgon Road at Oallen by two members of the public who had sighted the suitcase.

NSW Police said the pair "made the right decision" to report the matter to authorities.

Police in southern NSW initially treated the discovery as suspicious. (ABC News)

"They were affected yesterday and we will be in touch to let them know that it was not human remains."

Oallen is a small village on the Shoalhaven River in the Southern Tablelands, 109km north-east of Canberra and 254km south-west of Sydney.
